memoryText: My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 2 Corinthians 12:9 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These are the words of the Lord Jesus to Paul, spoken after he pleaded three times for relief from his thorn.

“My grace is sufficient for you.” The Lord does not say, “I will remove it,” but “My grace is enough.” Grace here means God’s favor and strength given to us in Christ. There is no situation in which it runs out. Paul needed daily grace, and so do we.

“For my power is made perfect in weakness.” Weakness is not an obstacle to God’s work but an opportunity for it. When we are strong in ourselves, we credit ourselves; when we are weak, the power of Christ is clearly seen. Paul went on to say, “I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me.”

This verse reverses the world’s logic. The world says to hide weakness and project strength. The gospel says to bring weakness to Christ. The cross itself is the great display of power in weakness.

When you are tired, limited, struggling with a thorn, or aware of your inadequacy, say this verse. Christ is not disappointed by your weakness; he is glorified in it. His grace is enough for today.
weekInReview: This week you finished the unit with 2 Corinthians. In chapters 1 to 3, Paul blessed God as the Father of mercies and God of all comfort, taught that all the promises of God find their Yes in Christ, and described the new covenant ministry of the Spirit that transforms us from one degree of glory to another. A doctrinal pause on death and the intermediate state showed that to be absent from the body is to be at home with the Lord. Chapters 4 and 5 spoke of the treasure in jars of clay, the inner self renewed day by day, the new creation, the ministry of reconciliation, and the great exchange in which Christ was made sin so that we might become the righteousness of God. Chapters 6 to 9 called us to holiness, godly grief, and cheerful generosity, grounded in Christ who became poor for our sake. Chapters 10 to 13 closed with Paul’s boasting in weakness, the thorn in the flesh, and the promise that Christ’s grace is sufficient. The unit review on Day 783 drew the three letters together around Galatians 2:20.
reflectionQuestions: Paul’s thorn was not removed, but he received grace. What weakness, limitation, or hardship in your life might God be using to display his power? How might you boast in it?
Second Corinthians 5:21 says Christ was made sin for us so that we might become the righteousness of God. What does it mean to you that your sin was counted to him and his righteousness to you?
Paul says we are ambassadors for Christ, entrusted with the message of reconciliation. Who in your life needs to hear it from you? What is one step you can take this week?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that his grace is sufficient.
Thank him that his power is made perfect in weakness.
